_comment: 🧩️ XLSX ECMA-376/✳️any's own contribution to the repository test platform — its mutation oracle registration and its declared mutation vocabulary (wave 7, ticket 26/08/23/END-TO-END-TESTING-REFACTOR). Discovered by convention alongside ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio's own top-level manifest; merged into one registry, no central edit required. Registers ONE oracle id for the reference PAIRING this subset needs (no single crate both reads and modifies an XLSX): `calamine` 0.36 parses a real workbook into resolved cell data; `rust_xlsxwriter` 0.96 assembles a brand-new package from a grid built out of that read — never opens and patches the original. Seven of the ten declared kinds (`no-mutation`, `set-snapshot`, `insert-sheet`, `remove-sheet`, `rename-sheet`, `set-cell`, `remove-cell`) are fully representable as 'read the whole workbook into a grid, change the grid, rebuild the whole workbook' and stay `@mode-differential`. The remaining three (`insert-shared-string`, `remove-shared-string`, `set-shared-string`) address the shared-string pool by an INDEX independent of any cell reference — the one axis neither crate exposes (`calamine`'s own `strings: Vec<String>` field and `read_shared_strings` method are both private; `rust_xlsxwriter`'s shared-string table is populated only as a byproduct of `write_string` on a cell, with no API to target an entry directly) — so their `mutate`/`inverse` scenarios are `@mode-round-trip`/`@mode-property` instead of `@mode-differential`; see the Feature file's own description and this subset's `🦀️oracle.rs` module doc comment for the full reasoning.

oracles.rationale: The reference ECMA-376 SpreadsheetML reader of the Rust ecosystem, paired with the reference writer `rust_xlsxwriter` 0.96 (MIT OR Apache-2.0, https://github.com/jmcnamara/rust_xlsxwriter), declared as this entry's linked `packages` member so the dependency ratchet and the oracle-purity probe classify it in its own right rather than only reading about it here for the seven mutation kinds this pairing can independently reproduce end to end (read the real workbook into a per-sheet cell grid, apply the change to the grid, rebuild the whole workbook from it — the only channel available, since `rust_xlsxwriter` cannot open and patch an existing package). Registered under `calamine` because every scenario's comparison runs through `calamine` as the independent reader on BOTH sides (oracle output and subject output alike), matching how this catalog's `@oracle-` tag names a single id per feature. `rust_xlsxwriter` is the paired producer for the differential kinds and is exercised by every green `@mode-differential` scenario even though it is not the package name on this entry; it is registered under this entry's `packages` list, which is what puts it inside the same test-only ratchet as `calamine`.

packages.role: independent SpreadsheetML writer — the producing half `calamine` does not have

comparisonProfiles.description: XLSX workbooks compared by their real per-sheet cell grid (sheet name, then every non-empty cell's row/col/resolved value, read independently by `calamine` on both sides) PLUS a caller-tracked `sharedStringCount` field — `calamine` exposes no accessor for the raw shared-string pool size (see this subset's `🦀️oracle.rs` module doc comment), so that one field is supplied by the case adapter rather than derived from the projected bytes: the oracle side by structural arithmetic on the applied kind, the subject side by reading its own real `XlsxWorkbook::shared_strings.len()`. `Number` cells carry a small floating-point tolerance since ECMA-376 stores every number as an IEEE-754 double and two independent writers may round the same value's textual form a few ULPs apart.
